Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Round structure 3 Playing cards 4 Card strength Goal The Granny must: Set the table (2 green tokens on the table) Cook Sarma (3 green tokens on the stove) Clean the house (no red tokens on the stove) Make the bed (2 green tokens on the bed) The Propuh wants: Open the door (2 red tokens on the door) Open the window (2 red tokens on the window) Note: if all cards are discarded Granny is tired and Propuh wins by default. Round structure Granny may move Granny figurine Granny plays a card Propuh plays a card Granny plays a card Propuh plays a card If the Propuh card is left on the table, discard it and place one Propuh token at its location Granny may remove one Propuh token from the location of the Granny figurine Deal 2 cards to Granny and Propuh If there are no cards left continue with the cards in hand. If there is only one card left (single player) do not deal it. Check if Granny or Propuh completed their goals If both Granny and Propuh have completed all their goals then Propuh wins If nobody won, start a new round Playing cards You can play a card on any one of the three locations. If you play a card on a location that has an unresolved card on it, you are attempting to counter it. If there is an unresolved card and you do not counter it, then the player who played the card discards it and places a token on that card location. You counter a card if you play a stronger card on the same location. If you do, discard both cards. If you do not, discard the card that was not countered and place a token in that location. Tokens mark your progress in each location. Players can place up to the maximum number of tokens indicated on that location, excess tokens are discarded. Card strength Any card played on the location of its suit is a trump card. If both or neither card are trumps, then the one with the higher numerical value is stronger. A strategic survival board game inspired by local superstition and card games.
Each player draws the cards in turn and combines them with each other or with the "Grandmothers" location on the board to achieve their goal. This creates simple gameplay with lots of options for both players.

Playing as the protagonist, you must complete a series of missions to win before your time is up or the notorious "Propuh" enters your house. 
Play your cards wisely because once the deck runs out, it is game over. 
Move the "Grandmother" to the most critical location inside the house to complete tasks easily or gain an advantage.

As for the second player (the antagonist), those playing the immaterial "Propuh" draw from the same deck of cards and attempt to get into the house. Once the "Propuh" is inside, it wins! 
In a single-player game, the "Propuh" is played by the game itself.

Note: Propuh is a crosswind (or draught) that blows through the house. It is a good thing in almost all of the world, but in some countries, it is considered a cause of many ailments.
You may not have any two windows, two doors, or a window and a door open at the same time, because it could kill you!

-description from designer

[Rating: 3/10] Not my kind of game, so no surprise I did not enjoy this. It's not really trick-taking, just deciding if you want to or even can counter your opponent's card.

[Rating: 3/10] A 2 player trick taking game where players take on roles trying to make their objectives. Players will play cards into 1 of the 3 spaces and if the card isn't displaced my an opponents higher card, they gain a token, likely closer to completing their objective.

[Rating: 5/10] The theme is what drew me in - the epic battle between Baba and Propuh. The game box turning into the game area is a nice touch and very on-theme. The cards can be hard to read due to the artwork and chosen font for the numbers clashing. Unfortunately, the gameplay was disappointing, it's not for me...

[Rating: 5/10] Rating is based on the 2p game and giving it a boost for it's tiny size and funky theme and illustration.  Simple "trick-taking" game where you are usually playing a card where it is trump (3 suits with 3 matching locations), but sometimes playing a non-trump card somewhere hoping the opponent can't beat it.  There's some hand management deciding what to play this round vs keep for next round - you start with a hand of 4, play 2, draw 2.  Interesting asymmetric win condition, but too simple for my taste.
